firewall.card.hint: Four inbound rules - TCP 8000 (the site), UDP and TCP 53 (the console's DNS) and TCP 443 (the guide's HTTPS). Each is added once and never again.
firewall.state.exists: inbound TCP 8000 rule is already there
firewall.state.declined: rule NOT added - the Windows elevation prompt was declined
firewall.state.unavailable: the firewall could not be checked on this system
firewall.note.declined: Hosting still works on this PC. Windows may block the console from reaching ports 8000, 53 and 443 - if the page never loads on the PS5, press TRY AGAIN and accept the prompt, or allow Pyre in Windows Defender Firewall for private networks.
firewall.note.failed: Hosting still works on this PC. Windows may block the console from reaching ports 8000, 53 and 443.
firewall.note.admin: Pyre runs unelevated. The rule is added by a one-off elevated helper, never on every launch.
howto.1: Run Pyre on this PC. The PC and the PS5 must be on the same network - same router, same Wi-Fi.
howto.2: Note the address shown above, then press START HOSTING.
howto.3: On the PS5: Settings → Network → Settings → Set Up Internet Connection → your network → Advanced Settings → DNS Settings → Manual, and set the DNS to the address from step 2.
howto.4: On the PS5 open the User's Guide - it opens the console's browser - and follow the guide on the page this PC is hosting. Pick RUN PYRE and keep the page open.
ps5.button: WHERE DO I GO ON THE PS5?
ps5.title: On the PS5
ps5.step.2: 2.  Settings - the gear icon at the top right of that bar.
ps5.step.3: 3.  "Guide & Tips, Health and Safety, and Other Information" - scroll down the Settings list to it and open it.
ps5.step.4: 4.  "Guide and Tips" - then choose "User's Guide". That opens the console's built-in browser.
ps5.step.5: 5.  It should land on the page this PC is hosting.
ps5.note: While hosting, Pyre answers DNS on port 53 and serves the guide over HTTPS on 443. Sony and PSN names are refused, and everything else goes through filtering resolvers, so the console keeps its internet without the ads.

emu.intro: Where the console expects files for the emulators already set up on it. Paths are shown as they appear over FTP, so the same path works in FileZilla.
emu.retro.intro: RetroArch runs from the console's internal storage, not a USB drive. Its menu front-end (ES-DE) reads games from the ROMs folder below.

emu.note: These are the folders as they are on this console. Pyre only reads them - it is a reference so you know where to drop files, not a setting.
cli.help: Pyre - PYRE PS5 self-host desktop tool
cli.usage:
Usage:
  Pyre.exe                          open the window (normal use)
  Pyre.exe --serve                 host with no window (diagnostics/automation)
  Pyre.exe --selftest              start the server, verify the unpacked site against the embedded manifest, then serve over real HTTP
  Pyre.exe --add-firewall-rule     one-off elevated action (launched by Pyre itself)
  Pyre.exe --check-firewall        report whether the inbound rule exists
cli.options:
Options:
  --root <dir>     serve this folder instead of the copy embedded in the exe (development/testing)
  --port <n>       port to bind (default 8000)
  --log <file>     also write output to this file
  --duration <sec> stop after this many seconds (0 = until killed)
  --no-firewall    never check or add the firewall rule this run
